# ADR-PTY-014 — Party identity with Customer and Supplier roles; credit terms on the Customer

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The project registry lists Customer, Supplier, Address and "Credit limit & terms" as PTY candidates (CAND-PTY-001 … 004) and leaves the owner of credit limits and terms open (OI-16: Party vs Settlements). The PRD cites module-registry decision 4 ("one Party identity record per counterparty … adding the other role is an action in place") and decision 6 (credit limit and terms per customer, with the "Customer credit exposure" extension point). The profile's master defaults (nameAr, nameEn, code, isActiveFl) would be duplicated if Customer and Supplier each held them.

## Decision
- ENT-PTY-001 Party (master, SHARED owner) holds names, code, mobile, email, tax registration number and active state once.
- ENT-PTY-002 Customer and ENT-PTY-003 Supplier (master, SHARED owner) are role records linked to the Party (at most one of each per Party); their standard name/code fields are presented from the Party, not held twice. The Party is inactive when no role is active.
- Credit limit and payment terms are fields of the Customer (not a separate entity); PTY owns them, resolving OI-16 for v1. Settlements reports open exposure into PTY (ADR-PTY-017).
- Payment terms are a whole number of days (0–365), not a lookup, so that Settlements can compute due dates without a lookup attribute. Supplier payment terms are flag-independent (ADR-PTY-012).
- ENT-PTY-004 Address is SHARED (owner) with SLS, PUR, SFR as the module registry states, overriding the project registry's earlier PRIVATE candidate.

## Consequences
- Consumers reference Customer or Supplier identifiers (HARD-FK) and read names through them.
- A trader who is both customer and supplier is one Party; contact changes appear in both roles.
- Payment terms codes (e.g. NET_30) are not offered in v1; a later version can add a lookup without changing the stored days.

## Traces
US-PTY-001, US-PTY-003, US-PTY-004, US-PTY-005, US-PTY-011 · ENT-PTY-001, ENT-PTY-002, ENT-PTY-003, ENT-PTY-004 · REQ-PTY-004, REQ-PTY-016, REQ-PTY-024 … REQ-PTY-029, REQ-PTY-064, REQ-PTY-065 · RULE-PTY-008, RULE-PTY-009

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-015 — Guest matching and conversion to a CUSTOMER-realm account

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
KB §3 D5 / DP §5 G9: the guest becomes a CUSTOMER-realm account after the first order. The PRD cites module-registry decision 5: a guest who is already a Customer is attached to that Customer and is linked "through a `sec` customer invitation, never by an unverified contact". The matching keys, the contact formats, how the account is created for a brand-new guest, and how ambiguous matches are handled were not stated.

## Decision
- Matching runs over active Parties only, excluding the walk-in Customer's Party: first by email (case-insensitive; email is unique among active Parties, D-03), then by mobile when exactly one active Party matches after normalisation (remove spaces and dashes, a leading "+" or "00").
- A match on a Party without a Customer adds a Customer (RETAIL). A match whose Customer is inactive is refused with a message that does not reveal the match. A mobile matching more than one Party creates a new Customer rather than guessing.
- Guest details never change a matched Party's names, contacts or addresses.
- Both for a new Customer and for a matched Customer without a linked user, PTY requests a CUSTOMER-realm invitation from given `sec` (SecCustomerInvitationApi) — for a matched Customer addressed to the contact recorded on the Party, not the one typed by the guest. `secUserId` is set only when `sec` reports the invitation accepted; one user links to one Customer.
- Contact formats: email = one "@", non-empty local part, domain with a "."; mobile = optional "+" and 7–15 digits (ITU-T E.164 maximum length).
- Guest details must carry an email or a mobile.

## Consequences
- No account is reached by typing someone else's contact; duplicates are avoided whenever the match is unambiguous.
- Shared family mobiles can still produce a second Customer; the Owner can merge manually in a later version.

## Traces
US-PTY-009, US-PTY-010 · ENT-PTY-001, ENT-PTY-002, ENT-PTY-004 · REQ-PTY-011, REQ-PTY-050 … REQ-PTY-063 · RULE-PTY-003, RULE-PTY-004, RULE-PTY-013, RULE-PTY-019, RULE-PTY-020, RULE-PTY-021

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-016 — Credit overrun approval as a PTY Credit override request

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
POL-PTY-008 and US-PTY-015 / US-PTY-016: a sale above the credit limit either warns or is blocked until a user holding the credit-override permission approves it; the default is block with override. The sale document belongs to SLS, which sits below PTY in the fixed DAG, so PTY cannot reference it. The Approvals module (APR) is wave 3, while PTY and SLS are wave 1. The profile forbids a workflow engine but allows a module-specific approval flow when a story explicitly asks for it.

## Decision
- PTY owns ENT-PTY-005 Credit override request (transactional, SHARED owner): docNo from given `sequence`, the Customer, sale amount, credit limit and open exposure at request, the credit-check result, and the sale held as a text reference (`sourceDocumentRef`).
- Single-step lifecycle (A7): PENDING → APPROVED → USED; PENDING → REJECTED (reason required); PENDING → CANCELLED (requester only). An APPROVED request covers one sale of the same Customer up to its amount.
- A request is accepted only under BLOCK_WITH_OVERRIDE for a result of OVER_LIMIT, NO_CREDIT or EXPOSURE_UNAVAILABLE, never for the walk-in Customer, and never while `b2bCredit` is off. Under WARN no request is needed.
- The credit-override permission is UPDATE on page PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE, held by the Owner preset (D-06); Seller/Cashier holds VIEW, CREATE and DELETE (cancel own). Approvers receive an in-app notification through given `notif`.
- The credit-overrun action is a tenant setting in given `cu`, values from lookup CREDIT_OVERRUN_ACTION; no PTY entity re-creates the setting.

## Consequences
- SLS and SFR call create / read / use on the request (A8.1) and keep the request id on their sale.
- If APR later offers generic approval steps, a later version can route the PENDING state through it without changing the request record.

## Traces
US-PTY-015, US-PTY-016, US-PTY-017 · ENT-PTY-005 · REQ-PTY-086 … REQ-PTY-105, REQ-PTY-107 · RULE-PTY-023, RULE-PTY-025 … RULE-PTY-029, RULE-PTY-031 … RULE-PTY-033

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-017 — Open exposure through contributors; credit check outcomes; flag switch-off answer

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
US-PTY-014 needs the Customer's open exposure before a credit sale. Receivables (STL) and open orders (SLS) live in modules that depend on PTY; the PRD cites the module-registry EXTENSION POINT "Customer credit exposure". US-PTY-013 needs `b2bCredit` switch-off to be blocked while credit data exists, but the owner of the capability-flag switch is still OPEN (registry OI-05, P-02).

## Decision
- PTY declares the credit exposure contribution: every downstream module that holds exposure registers as a contributor and reports a Customer's open exposure; PTY sums them, and uses 0 when none is registered (so PTY is usable before STL ships).
- A contributor that does not answer within 3 seconds makes the result EXPOSURE_UNAVAILABLE (never WITHIN_LIMIT on incomplete data).
- An empty credit limit means no credit allowance: the result is NO_CREDIT (the walk-in Customer always gets NO_CREDIT).
- Results come from lookup CREDIT_CHECK_RESULT: WITHIN_LIMIT, OVER_LIMIT, NO_CREDIT, EXPOSURE_UNAVAILABLE, NOT_APPLICABLE (flag off). Every non-WITHIN result carries the tenant's credit-overrun action and whether an approved request is required.
- PTY answers the flag owner's switch-off question with the number of Customers carrying a credit limit or payment terms; a count above 0 refuses the switch-off with a message and a next action (open the Customer credit list filtered to those Customers).

## Consequences
- STL and SLS each implement one contributor in their own SRS; their XM edges point to PTY.
- The 3-second limit is a default; P3.1 may tune it without changing the outcome rule.
- Whichever module P-02 assigns as the flag owner calls PTY's dependency answer.

## Traces
US-PTY-011, US-PTY-012, US-PTY-013, US-PTY-014 · ENT-PTY-002 · REQ-PTY-068, REQ-PTY-074 … REQ-PTY-085 · RULE-PTY-024

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-018 — Physical precision of fields the SRS leaves open

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P2 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Filed   : verbatim from the db-script §5.2 (analysis/modules/PTY/P2/db-script-pty.md) by the P3.1 repair, ADR-PTY-030

## Context
SRS A3 types creditLimit, saleAmount, creditLimitAtRequest and openExposure as `decimal` without precision, paymentTermDays as `number (0 – 365)` (a type the syntax map lacks), and the lookup-code fields as `lookup` without length. The platform serves Egypt and the Gulf, where some base currencies (OMR, KWD, BHD) carry 3 minor-unit decimals.

## Decision
Monetary decimals → `NUMERIC(18,3)` (15 integer digits, 3 decimals — covers every base currency of the target markets). Whole-number days → `INTEGER`, declared once in the script header. Lookup code columns → `VARCHAR(50)` (longest seeded code: EXPOSURE_UNAVAILABLE, 20 characters; room for open-lookup values added as data).

## Consequences
A 2-decimal currency stores a trailing zero digit; the backend rounds to the tenant currency's minor unit. No SRS meaning changes.

## Traces
ENT-PTY-002.creditLimit, ENT-PTY-002.paymentTermDays, ENT-PTY-003.paymentTermDays, ENT-PTY-005.saleAmount / creditLimitAtRequest / openExposure, DBF-PTY-014, 015, 016, 026, 034, 051, 052, 053, 054, 063; REQ-PTY-064, REQ-PTY-065, REQ-PTY-091.

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-019 — Audit user columns hold the platform principal

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P2 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Filed   : verbatim from the db-script §5.2 (analysis/modules/PTY/P2/db-script-pty.md) by the P3.1 repair, ADR-PTY-030

## Context
SRS A3 lists createdBy / updatedBy as "reference (given sec User, BIGINT)", system-filled. The engine's AUDIT COLUMNS rule (from the given) states that audit user columns are filled by the platform and hold a principal string, not a numeric FK; the given's auditing fills them, and a business module never writes them.

## Decision
CREATED_BY and UPDATED_BY are `VARCHAR(100)` holding the principal the given `sec` module authenticates — the same sec User the SRS refers to, in the form the platform writes. Non-audit user references the module itself sets keep the SRS type: SEC_USER_ID (DBF-PTY-017) and DECIDED_BY (DBF-PTY-056) are `BIGINT` sec user identifiers.

## Consequences
RULE-PTY-029 ("only the requester cancels") compares PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUEST.CREATED_BY with the current principal; REQ-PTY-102 filters on it (indexed, IDX_PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUEST_CREATED_BY). User names shown in history and decisions are resolved through SecUserDirectoryApi (SRS A9). No constraint on SEC_USER either way, so no SRS behaviour changes.

## Traces
ENT-PTY-001 … ENT-PTY-005 .createdBy / .updatedBy; DBF-PTY-009, 011, 021, 023, 029, 031, 046, 048, 064, 066; REQ-PTY-096, REQ-PTY-102; RULE-PTY-029.

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-020 — No currency column on PTY amounts (profile check CM-8)

Status  : SUPERSEDED by ADR-PTY-037 (gate-analysis revise, G11; was ACCEPTED, non-breaking) · Stage : P2 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Filed   : verbatim from the db-script §5.2 (analysis/modules/PTY/P2/db-script-pty.md) by the P3.1 repair, ADR-PTY-030

## Context
Profile check CM-8 asks every monetary row to carry its currency. PTY holds amounts on ENT-PTY-002 (creditLimit) and ENT-PTY-005 (saleAmount, creditLimitAtRequest, openExposure). The approved SRS states a business-policies SCOPE EXCEPTION — "multi-currency party balances" — and types each amount as "tenant base currency"; no currency field exists in SRS A3. NO-COLUMN-INVENTION forbids a column with no SRS origin.

## Decision
No currency column. The amounts are thresholds and approval amounts expressed in the tenant base currency (held by the given `cu`), as the SRS and the contract's §0 rules ("Currency: every amount is in the tenant's base currency") promise. PTY carries no stock-bearing row and no price, so the warehouse and price-list parts of CM-8 do not apply.

## Consequences
Consumers convert a foreign-currency document to base currency before a credit check (CON-PTY-015) and a request (CON-PTY-016). Lifting the scope exception in a later version adds a currency column per amount as an ADDITIVE migration with its own SRS field.

## Traces
ENT-PTY-002.creditLimit, ENT-PTY-005.saleAmount; DBF-PTY-015, 051, 052, 053; REQ-PTY-064, REQ-PTY-079, REQ-PTY-091.

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-021 — Tenant scoping without a tenant column

Status  : SUPERSEDED by ADR-PTY-035 (gate-analysis revise, G2; was ACCEPTED, non-breaking) · Stage : P2 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Filed   : verbatim from the db-script §5.2 (analysis/modules/PTY/P2/db-script-pty.md) by the P3.1 repair, ADR-PTY-030

## Context
RULE-PTY-002, RULE-PTY-014 and RULE-PTY-020 are per-tenant uniqueness rules. The SRS has no tenant field; business modules are tenant-agnostic and the given `erp-core` (CORE_TENANT, TenantContext) isolates tenants (platform brief §0, D3).

## Decision
No tenant column (NO-COLUMN-INVENTION). Every uniqueness rule is declared once in the script (UQ_PTY_PARTY_EMAIL, UQ_PTY_CUSTOMER_IS_WALK_IN_FL, UQ_PTY_CUSTOMER_SEC_USER_ID, UQ_PTY_PARTY_CODE, UQ_PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUEST_DOC_NO, UQ_PTY_ADDRESS_PARTY_CODE) and holds per tenant under the isolation the given applies to every business table.

## Consequences
If the given isolates tenants by a discriminator column in shared tables, the given's tenancy mechanism adds that column to each PTY table and leads each UNIQUE above with it; that is the given's documented integration, applied by the executor in P3.1, not a PTY column. Nothing in PTY reads a tenant identifier.

## Traces
RULE-PTY-002, RULE-PTY-014, RULE-PTY-020; DBF-PTY-003, 007, 017, 018, 061; REQ-PTY-010, REQ-PTY-044, REQ-PTY-054.

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-022 — Lookup seed rows written against the given mdl tables

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) — column list and TENANT_ID = 1 revised by ADR-PTY-035 · Stage : P2 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Filed   : verbatim from the db-script §5.2 (analysis/modules/PTY/P2/db-script-pty.md) by the P3.1 repair, ADR-PTY-030

## Context
PTY owns five lookup keys (SRS A6); their values live in the given `mdl` tables MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE and MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE, which this script must seed and must not re-create (engine §4.2). The given's internal column list is not among this stage's inputs.

## Decision
BLOCK 8 seeds both tables with the column list CODE, NAME_AR, NAME_EN, IS_ACTIVE_FL (type) and LOOKUP_TYPE_CODE, CODE, NAME_AR, NAME_EN, SORT_ORDER, IS_ACTIVE_FL (value) — the platform naming convention for a coded, bilingual, deactivatable lookup — inserted idempotently with `WHERE NOT EXISTS`. The values and labels are verbatim from SRS A6.

## Consequences
The executor of the backend plan (P3.1) checks this column list against the given's installed `mdl` DDL when it turns BLOCK 8 into the module's Flyway migration (V1000+) and aligns the column names if the given's differ; the seeded keys and values are fixed by the SRS and do not change. New tenants receive the values through the given's provisioning copy of `mdl` seeds.

## Traces
SRS A6 (CUSTOMER_GROUP, ADDRESS_TYPE, CREDIT_OVERRUN_ACTION, CREDIT_CHECK_RESULT, CREDIT_OVERRIDE_STATUS); DBF-PTY-014, 034, 054, 063; REQ-PTY-007, REQ-PTY-038, REQ-PTY-040, REQ-PTY-086, REQ-PTY-091.

# ADR-PTY-023 — ADR sequence continued after the db-script's recorded decisions

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The P3.1 brief states that the next free ADR id is ADR-PTY-018, counted from the files present in `analysis/decisions/PTY/` (ADR-PTY-001 … ADR-PTY-017). The current db-script (P2) and its registry, however, already record five decisions under ADR-PTY-018 … ADR-PTY-022 (physical precision, audit principal columns, no currency column, tenant scoping without a tenant column, lookup seed against the given mdl tables) and state "Next free ADR : ADR-PTY-023". Those five were recorded in full inside the db-script for the orchestrator to file, and no file exists for them yet. Writing new decisions under ADR-PTY-018 … 022 would give two different decisions the same id.

## Decision
- This stage raises its decisions from ADR-PTY-023 onwards, so that no id already used by the db-script is reused.
- The plan applies the five P2 decisions exactly as the db-script states them, and cites them as "the db-script §5.2 decisions" rather than by id, because their files do not exist on disk.
- Filing ADR-PTY-018 … ADR-PTY-022 under `analysis/decisions/PTY/` from the db-script's §5.2 text is left to the orchestrator, which owns that step. This stage does not write those files, because it does not own them.

## Consequences
- ADR ids stay unique and continuous with the current state: ADR-PTY-023 … ADR-PTY-029 are raised here, and the next free id is ADR-PTY-030.
- Until the P2 files are filed, a reader of `analysis/decisions/PTY/` sees a gap at 018 … 022. The db-script remains the authoritative text of those five decisions.

## Traces
backend-execution-plan-pty.md (Decisions) · registry-exec-be-pty.md (ADRs) · db-script §5.2 · registry-db "Next free ADR"

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-PTY-024.md>>>
# ADR-PTY-024 — Error Catalog: PLATFORM-STD rows, status mapping and slugs

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The engine requires infrastructure errors (malformed request, unauthenticated, forbidden, not found, server failure) to be Error Catalog rows with rule `PLATFORM-STD` and an ADR. The SRS gives no message text for them. The SRS also does not say which HTTP status each business rule maps to. The profile fixes the code format `{MOD}-{http}[-{SLUG}]` and the statuses the platform can emit (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 415, 422, 500).

## Decision
- **Status mapping for rule rows.**
  - 422: a rule that refuses the content of a request (format, range, required value, lookup value, flag off, state that the caller can fix).
  - 409: a rule that refuses because of other data that already exists — RULE-PTY-002 email taken, RULE-PTY-009 role held, RULE-PTY-026 request no longer pending.
  - 403: RULE-PTY-029 (only the requester cancels), because it is an authorisation outcome.
  - 500: RULE-PTY-030 (audit not recorded), because it is a server-side failure that the caller can only retry.
- **Slugs.** Upper-case words that name the meaning (e.g. `PTY-422-NAME-REQUIRED`). They are stable, because downstream stages cite the code and not the text.
- **PLATFORM-STD rows and their messages:**
  - PTY-400-VALIDATION — «الطلب غير صالح: تحقّق من الحقول المرسلة.» / "The request is not valid: check the submitted fields."
  - PTY-401-UNAUTHENTICATED — «سجّل الدخول للمتابعة.» / "Sign in to continue."
  - PTY-403-FORBIDDEN — «ليست لديك صلاحية لتنفيذ هذا الإجراء.» / "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  - PTY-404-CUSTOMER-NOT-FOUND — «العميل غير موجود.» / "The customer was not found."
  - PTY-404-SUPPLIER-NOT-FOUND — «المورّد غير موجود.» / "The supplier was not found."
  - PTY-404-PARTY-NOT-FOUND — «الطرف غير موجود.» / "The party was not found."
  - PTY-404-ADDRESS-NOT-FOUND — «العنوان غير موجود.» / "The address was not found."
  - PTY-404-CREDIT-OVERRIDE-NOT-FOUND — «طلب تجاوز حد الائتمان غير موجود.» / "The credit override request was not found."
  - PTY-500-INTERNAL — «حدث خطأ غير متوقع. أعد المحاولة.» / "An unexpected error occurred. Try again."
- A record of another tenant reads as not found.
- No row describes a network failure, because the platform is one deployable and PTY calls only in-process interfaces.

## Consequences
- Every operation of `api-spec-pty.yaml` answers 400, 401, 403 and 500. The global search (API-PTY-027) is the exception for 403: it answers an empty list instead (REQ-PTY-043).
- The texts of the PLATFORM-STD rows are this module's defaults. If the given erp-core publishes platform-wide texts for these statuses, the executor may use them, but the codes do not change.

## Traces
backend-execution-plan-pty.md §Error Catalog · REQ-PTY-043, REQ-PTY-090 · RULE-PTY-002, RULE-PTY-009, RULE-PTY-026, RULE-PTY-029, RULE-PTY-030

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-PTY-025.md>>>
# ADR-PTY-025 — Permissions the SRS leaves open; in-process callers; invitation-handler outcomes

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) — in-process callers and the Address permission revised by ADR-PTY-039; the invitation outcomes by the backend plan CORE (outbox subscriber) · Stage : P3.1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The SRS access matrices (B4) give permissions per screen and action. Several endpoints are not covered:
- the operations offered to consuming modules (SRS A8.1): walk-in Customer, guest resolution, credit check, use of an approval, the `b2bCredit` switch-off answer;
- reactivation;
- Address endpoints, which are shared by the Customers and Suppliers screens;
- clearing credit on a page that grants no DELETE;
- reading a single Credit override request.

The SRS also requires two outcomes of the CUSTOMER-realm invitation acceptance — RULE-PTY-013 and RULE-PTY-020 — to be "reported". That acceptance arrives in-process from the given sec module, not over HTTP. The platform is one deployable (`module_interface: in_process`).

## Decision
- **Reactivation** (API-PTY-005, API-PTY-010) requires the DELETE permission of the page. Reactivation is the reverse of deactivation, and the SRS names the Owner as the actor of both.
- **Address endpoints** (API-PTY-011 … 015, 029, 012):
  - Writes require UPDATE on PTY_CUSTOMER when the Party holds a Customer, or UPDATE on PTY_SUPPLIER when it holds a Supplier (SRS B4: "Address create, update and deactivation require UPDATE on this page"). The controller checks that the caller has either permission. The service then checks the permission that matches the roles the Party holds.
  - Reads require VIEW on either page.
- **Clear credit** (API-PTY-018) requires PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_CREDIT_UPDATE. It clears two fields, and the page grants no DELETE.
- **Operations for consuming modules:**
  - Walk-in Customer (API-PTY-033) and credit check (API-PTY-035) require PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_VIEW, which the seller performing a sale holds.
  - Guest resolution (API-PTY-034) requires PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_CREATE for a REST caller.
  - Use of an approval (API-PTY-036) requires PERM_PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_CREATE, the requester's permission.
  - The switch-off answer (API-PTY-037) requires PERM_PTY_CREDIT_SETTINGS_VIEW, which is held by the Owner, who switches flags.
- **Global search** (API-PTY-027) checks VIEW in the service. A caller without VIEW receives an empty list, not a 403 (REQ-PTY-043).
- **Reading a single request** (API-PTY-020) follows REQ-PTY-102. A caller without PERM_PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_UPDATE reads only requests it created. Any other request answers not found, so its existence is not revealed.
- **In-process callers.** A consuming module that calls `PtyPartyApi` authorises its own caller against its own permissions before it calls PTY — for example, the storefront for its anonymous shopper. PTY applies tenancy but does not re-check a PTY permission on the in-process path. The REST path keeps the permission above.
- **Invitation acceptance.** `CustomerInvitationAcceptanceHandler` returns an outcome to the given's callback: LINKED, or REFUSED together with the RULE-PTY-013 / RULE-PTY-020 message in ar + en. These outcomes have no HTTP status and no Error Catalog row. The database backstops them with CHK_PTY_CUSTOMER_WALK_IN_SEC_USER and UQ_PTY_CUSTOMER_SEC_USER_ID.

## Consequences
- The permission matrix grants only the actions B4 grants. CREATE and DELETE on PTY_CUSTOMER_CREDIT stay ungranted, and so do CREATE and DELETE on PTY_CREDIT_SETTINGS.
- If the given erp-core later provides a caller authority for in-process reads, the in-process path can adopt it without changing any signature.
- A custom role that needs the credit check without Customer VIEW is not supported in v1.

## Traces
API-PTY-005, 010, 011 … 015, 018, 020, 027, 029, 033 … 037 · REQ-PTY-015, REQ-PTY-021, REQ-PTY-043, REQ-PTY-052, REQ-PTY-054, REQ-PTY-102 · RULE-PTY-013, RULE-PTY-020 · SCR-REQ-PTY-001 … 005 (B4)

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-026 — Concurrency guards; Address default on a type change

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
Several PTY writes decide on a value they have just read:
- the next Address ordinal;
- whether a new Address is the first of its type;
- whether a role is the Party's last active role;
- whether a Party already holds a role;
- the status of a Credit override request;
- whether the walk-in Customer exists;
- whether a guest's email already belongs to a Party.

Two simultaneous requests can both read and both pass. The db-script has no version column, so optimistic locking is not available. The SRS also does not say what happens to the default flag when an Address's type is changed.

## Decision
- **The Party row is the mutex** for everything scoped to one Party: role add, active-state derivation, Address ordinal, and default switching. QR-PTY-001 runs `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. Locks are always taken Party first, then the child row, so no two transactions can deadlock on them.
- **Unique constraints and indexes of the db-script are the backstop** and are translated to catalog errors:
  - UQ_PTY_PARTY_EMAIL → PTY-409-EMAIL-TAKEN, naming the code of the Party that holds the email;
  - UQ_PTY_CUSTOMER_PARTY_FK and UQ_PTY_SUPPLIER_PARTY_FK → PTY-409-ROLE-HELD;
  - UQ_PTY_ADDRESS_PARTY_CODE and UQ_PTY_ADDRESS_IS_DEFAULT_FL → PTY-500-INTERNAL, which cannot happen under the Party lock.
- **Credit override transitions:** the row is locked (QR-PTY-033) and updated by compare-and-set on STATUS_CODE (QR-PTY-034). If the update changes no row, the request is re-read and RULE-PTY-026 (decisions) or RULE-PTY-028 (use) is returned.
- **Credit edits** lock the Customer row (QR-PTY-006), so every audit event's old value is the value the previous edit committed.
- **Walk-in Customer:**
  - creation runs in a REQUIRES_NEW transaction;
  - a violation of UQ_PTY_CUSTOMER_IS_WALK_IN_FL rolls back that transaction, including the Party row it created;
  - the existing walk-in Customer is then re-read and returned.
- **Guest resolution:**
  - Creation runs in a REQUIRES_NEW transaction.
  - If UQ_PTY_PARTY_EMAIL is violated, the matching is retried once, and the order attaches to the Party that won.
  - Mobile is not unique (SRS D-03), so two simultaneous mobile-only guests may create two Parties. This is the outcome REQ-PTY-061 already prescribes for an ambiguous mobile.
- **Business numbers** (Party code, docNo) are allocated atomically by the given NumberSeriesApi, backstopped by their unique constraints.
- **Address type change on update** (API-PTY-013):
  - If the Address was the default of its old type, it stops being the default. The most recently updated remaining active Address of the old type becomes the default, as when a default is deactivated (RULE-PTY-017).
  - In its new type, the Address becomes the default only if that type has no active Address.
- **Setting a default on an inactive Address** is refused as PTY-404-ADDRESS-NOT-FOUND, because an inactive Address cannot be the active default.

## Consequences
- Writes to one Party are serialised. This is acceptable, because a Party is edited by one user at a time in practice.
- No version column is needed. If one is added in a later version, the locks above may be replaced by optimistic checks without changing the API.

## Traces
QR-PTY-001, 004, 006, 008, 021, 024, 028, 029, 030, 033, 034, 036, 037 · API-PTY-001, 003 … 006, 008 … 011, 013 … 015, 017, 021 … 023, 033, 034, 036 · REQ-PTY-027, REQ-PTY-028, REQ-PTY-034, REQ-PTY-036, REQ-PTY-046, REQ-PTY-061, REQ-PTY-098, REQ-PTY-099 · RULE-PTY-002, RULE-PTY-009, RULE-PTY-014, RULE-PTY-017, RULE-PTY-026, RULE-PTY-028

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-027 — Query strategy: Party join, native normalised search and matching

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The engine's join governance says single-table responses do not join, and that any join or native query needs an ADR. Customer and Supplier hold no names and no code of their own: the SRS "presents" them from the Party, and the db-script stores them only on PTY_PARTY (ADR-PTY-014, REQ-PTY-024). The global search must compare without letter case and with Arabic letter forms unified (REQ-PTY-042). Guest matching compares normalised mobiles (ADR-PTY-015). The db-script installs no database extension.

## Decision
- **Party join.** Every read or search of a role joins PTY_PARTY on the role's PARTY_FK to return code, nameAr, nameEn, mobile, email and taxRegistrationNo. This applies to QR-PTY-005, 010, 012, 013, 015 and 020. Credit override reads and searches (QR-PTY-032, 035) join PTY_CUSTOMER and PTY_PARTY to show the Customer's code and names. All joins use intra-module FK paths. Lookup labels are never joined; the client resolves codes through the given mdl.
- **Global search (QR-PTY-011)** is a native query:
  - Arabic is unified with `TRANSLATE(x, 'أإآةى', 'اااهي')` on both sides, and the remaining text with `LOWER`.
  - Mobile is compared after `REGEXP_REPLACE(MOBILE, '[ -]', '', 'g')`.
  - Results are ordered by an exact code match first, then by the display name in the request language (falling back to the other language), and limited to 10.
- **Guest matching:**
  - Email (QR-PTY-036) is compared as `LOWER(BTRIM(EMAIL))`, the same expression as UQ_PTY_PARTY_EMAIL, so the index serves it.
  - Mobile (QR-PTY-037) is a native query that removes spaces and dashes and maps a leading "00" to "+". It reads `LIMIT 2`, because only "exactly one" versus "more than one" matters.
- No pg_trgm, unaccent or other extension is used. Search performance relies on the db-script's B-tree indexes and the bounded result size.

## Consequences
- For large tenants, "contains" searches scan the joined rows. If profiling demands it, a later version may add trigram indexes, which is a platform decision about extensions.
- The normalisation rules sit in one query each, and the in-process and REST paths share them.

## Traces
QR-PTY-005, 010, 011, 012, 013, 015, 020, 032, 035, 036, 037 · REQ-PTY-013, REQ-PTY-018, REQ-PTY-024, REQ-PTY-041, REQ-PTY-042, REQ-PTY-055, REQ-PTY-056, REQ-PTY-101 · ADR-PTY-014, ADR-PTY-015

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-028 — Credit computation and derived properties

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
Several values the SRS returns have no column: open exposure, projected exposure, available credit, credit check result, approval-required, the credit-overrun action, carries-credit, and credit history. The SRS does not say:
- whether the server trusts a caller-supplied credit check result when a Credit override request is created;
- whether a request may be created under WARN;
- how the 3-second contributor limit works on a single deployable;
- whether the walk-in Customer appears on the Customer credit list.

## Decision
- **Open exposure** is the sum of `CustomerCreditExposureContributor.openExposure(customerId)` over every registered bean, and 0 when there is none. Each contributor is an in-process call, invoked asynchronously with a 3-second time budget. A timeout or exception from any contributor makes the exposure unavailable. This is a time limit on a local call, not a network timeout, so no catalog row exists for it.
- **Credit check algorithm:**
  1. If the flag is off → NOT_APPLICABLE.
  2. If the credit limit is empty → NO_CREDIT.
  3. If the exposure is unavailable → EXPOSURE_UNAVAILABLE, with openExposure empty.
  4. If projected exposure (open exposure + sale amount) ≤ limit → WITHIN_LIMIT.
  5. Otherwise → OVER_LIMIT.

  OVER_LIMIT, NO_CREDIT and EXPOSURE_UNAVAILABLE carry the overrun action (default BLOCK_WITH_OVERRIDE), and approvalRequired = (action = BLOCK_WITH_OVERRIDE).
- **Creating a request recomputes the check on the server** and ignores any result the caller holds. The request stores the recomputed result, the limit at request and the open exposure. If the recomputed result is WITHIN_LIMIT, creation is refused with RULE-PTY-025.
- **A request may be created under WARN.** No rule forbids it and it harms nothing: approval is simply not required then.
- **Available credit** = credit limit − open exposure. It is empty when either value is empty.
- **carriesCredit** = credit limit or payment terms is non-empty. It is used by the credit list filter and the switch-off count.
- **The walk-in Customer is not listed on the Customer credit list**, because it can never carry credit (RULE-PTY-011). Inactive Customers are listed, so that their credit can be cleared before the flag is switched off.
- **Credit history** is read from the given AuditApi: the events of the Customer for the two fields, newest first. User names are resolved through SecUserDirectoryApi. PTY keeps no history table.
- **The credit-overrun action** is the tenant setting `PTY_CREDIT_OVERRUN_ACTION` in the given cu module (ADR-PTY-029).

## Consequences
- A sale can never be approved against a result that the caller computed on stale data.
- When a contributor is slow, credit sales fall back to the overrun handling and are never passed as within the limit.

## Traces
API-PTY-016, 019, 030, 031, 035, 037 · REQ-PTY-068, REQ-PTY-069, REQ-PTY-074, REQ-PTY-079 … REQ-PTY-089, REQ-PTY-091, REQ-PTY-104, REQ-PTY-108 · RULE-PTY-011, RULE-PTY-025 · ADR-PTY-017

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-029 — Bootstrap: number series, setting key, role grants, walk-in provisioning

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) — number series and the notification template revised by ADR-PTY-036 (seeded by the migration) · Stage : P3.1 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
PTY cannot answer its first calls until certain things exist:
- two number series (Party code, request docNo);
- a settings key for the credit-overrun action;
- the role grants of its five pages;
- the walk-in Customer.

The SRS gives the number formats only by example (P-000120, CO-000031). It names no series codes and no settings key. The db-script writes no rows to the given number-series or settings tables (its D-P2-07). Registering a page and deriving its permissions is not a grant: without grants, every endpoint would answer forbidden to every caller.

## Decision
- **Number series:**
  - `PTY_PARTY` — prefix `P-`, 6 digits, for DBF-PTY-007.
  - `PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE` — prefix `CO-`, 6 digits, for DBF-PTY-061.

  Both are registered through NumberSeriesApi by PTY's TenantProvisioningContributor for every provisioned tenant. Tenants provisioned before PTY was enabled get the same registration on PTY's startup migration path. The executor confirms the exact NumberSeriesApi registration operation against the erp-core-usage skill.
- **Setting:** `PTY_CREDIT_OVERRUN_ACTION`, stored through the given SettingsApi. It is not seeded: BLOCK_WITH_OVERRIDE applies until the Owner saves a value (REQ-PTY-087).
- **Pages and grants:** PTY's PermissionContributor declares the five pages, together with default grants to the preset roles exactly as SRS B4 lists them:
  - Owner — every listed action;
  - Seller/Cashier — PTY_CUSTOMER VIEW/CREATE/UPDATE, PTY_CUSTOMER_CREDIT VIEW, PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE VIEW/CREATE/DELETE;
  - Warehouse — PTY_SUPPLIER VIEW.

  The three credit pages are bound to the flag `b2bCredit` for menu visibility.
- **Walk-in Customer:** created by WalkInCustomerService.ensure. This runs from the TenantProvisioningContributor at provisioning (REQ-PTY-044), and on first demand for older tenants (REQ-PTY-046).
- **Lookup keys:** seeded by the db-script BLOCK 8 in PTY's Flyway migration. New tenants receive them through the given's mdl provisioning copy.

## Consequences
- The `bootstrap` block of the plan lists every row, together with who produces it.
- Customers and suppliers share one Party series, because the code belongs to the Party (SRS D-01 allows separate series later as an override).

## Traces
DBF-PTY-007, DBF-PTY-061 · REQ-PTY-006, REQ-PTY-044, REQ-PTY-046, REQ-PTY-070, REQ-PTY-087, REQ-PTY-092 · RULE-PTY-007, RULE-PTY-031 · SCR-REQ-PTY-001 … 005 (B4)

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-030 — P2 decisions ADR-PTY-018 … ADR-PTY-022 filed from the db-script §5.2

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 (repair round 1) · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The db-script and registry-db cite ADR-PTY-018 … ADR-PTY-022, and they record those five decisions in full in db-script §5.2 "for the orchestrator to file". No file existed for them in `analysis/decisions/PTY/`, so `gov.py analyze` refused the stage (C7.13 refs-exist, 10 CRITICAL findings). ADR-PTY-023 had left the filing to the orchestrator. This stage cannot edit the db-script, so the citations cannot be removed from the side that makes them.

## Decision
- File ADR-PTY-018 … ADR-PTY-022 under `analysis/decisions/PTY/`. Each file copies the db-script §5.2 text word for word (Context · Decision · Consequences · Traces · Status) and names the P2 stage as its origin. No decision is changed or added.
- This does not rewrite an existing ADR: none of the five ids had a file. ADR-PTY-023 stays as it is. Its third bullet ("left to the orchestrator") is superseded by this ADR for those five files only.

## Consequences
- Every ADR the db-script, registry-db and this plan cite now exists on disk. The ADR stream 001 … 032 has no gap.
- The db-script remains the text these files were copied from. If a later P2 version amends one of these decisions, it is recorded as a new ADR, never by editing these files.

## Traces
db-script §5.2 · registry-db (Decisions) · ADR-PTY-023 · backend-execution-plan-pty.md (Decisions) · registry-exec-be-pty.md (ADRs)

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-031 — Typed bodies for the reactivation and set-default PATCH endpoints

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 (repair round 1) · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
SRS B5 lists three PATCH operations whose only input is the path id: reactivate Customer (`/customers/{id}/activation`, API-PTY-005), reactivate Supplier (`/suppliers/{id}/activation`, API-PTY-010) and set default Address (`/parties/{partyId}/addresses/{id}/default`, API-PTY-015). PATCH means a partial update (engine §2A.2), and `gov.py analyze` (C7.31 api-spec-valid) refuses a PATCH with no typed `requestBody` schema. The SRS paths and verbs stay as they are.

## Decision
- Each of the three PATCH endpoints takes a required JSON body that names the one field it changes, with a value fixed by the endpoint's single meaning:
  - API-PTY-005 / API-PTY-010 — `ActivationRequest { isActiveFl: true }` (DBF-PTY-020 / DBF-PTY-028). Deactivation stays the DELETE of the resource (API-PTY-004 / API-PTY-009). The field is fixed to `true` so the same state change is not reachable through two endpoints with different rules (RULE-PTY-006, RULE-PTY-010).
  - API-PTY-015 — `DefaultAddressRequest { isDefaultFl: true }` (DBF-PTY-040). A default is cleared only by marking another Address of the same type (RULE-PTY-017).
- In the API document the field is `{type: boolean, const: true}` and `additionalProperties: false`. A missing body, a missing field or the value `false` is answered with the existing PTY-400-VALIDATION row (PLATFORM-STD, ADR-PTY-024). No new catalog row is added.

## Consequences
- The body states in the request what the PATCH changes, and the generated client and mock server type it. Behaviour, permissions, orchestration and errors of the three endpoints are otherwise unchanged.
- The frontend sends `{"isActiveFl": true}` / `{"isDefaultFl": true}` with these calls.

## Traces
API-PTY-005, API-PTY-010, API-PTY-015 · REQ-PTY-015, REQ-PTY-021, REQ-PTY-035 · DBF-PTY-020, DBF-PTY-028, DBF-PTY-040 · RULE-PTY-017 · api-spec-pty.yaml (ActivationRequest, DefaultAddressRequest)

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-032 — The XM total counts the XM ids the db-script names

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.1 (repair round 1) · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The plan's `totals` block must state `XM` as "the number of distinct `XM-*` ids in `db-script`" (engine §3; profile `declared_totals`, analyze `count-agrees`). The db-script's XM register is `records: []`, and no edge exists (SRS A8 `consumes: []`). Its §6 registry content does name one XM id, `XM-PTY-001`, as the *next free* XM id. `gov.py analyze` counts that id, so it refused `XM: 0` (C7.18, MAJOR). This stage cannot edit the db-script, where the wording would otherwise be fixed.

## Decision
- `totals` states `XM: 1`, the number of distinct `XM-*` ids the db-script carries, as the totals rule defines it.
- The plan says once, directly below the block, that this one id is the next-free pointer and that there are 0 integration edges. The header and the registry describe edges as "integration edges 0" or "XM register empty" rather than as an `XM` count, so no second statement of the total disagrees with the block.
- Nothing else changes: the register has no record, `INT-C` carries no block, and this stage mints no XM.

## Consequences
- A reader of `totals` alone sees 1. The note under the block and this ADR say it is a named id, not an edge.
- The db-script owner (P2) can avoid this in a later version by not naming the next-free XM id when the register is empty. The total then returns to 0 without any change to this plan's meaning.

## Traces
backend-execution-plan-pty.md (`totals`, Index) · registry-exec-be-pty.md (Integration, Event) · db-script §3 (`xm-register`), §6 · registry-db (Sequences)

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-033 — Credit values on the Customer screen: read-only, edited on Customer credit

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.2 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The SRS states two things about credit fields on the Customer screen (SCR-REQ-PTY-001 → SCR-PTY-001):
- SCR-REQ-PTY-001 B3 (Input), verbatim: "Credit fields are not on this screen; they belong to SCR-REQ-PTY-003 (REQ-PTY-070)."
- AC-PTY-082 (REQ-PTY-073), verbatim: "the Customer screen shows the creditLimit and paymentTermDays fields, the menu shows Customer credit, Credit override requests and Credit control settings, and 0 setup steps are presented".
- AC-PTY-078 (REQ-PTY-070), verbatim: "the Customer screen shows 0 credit fields and 0 credit filters" (flag off).

Read as written, B3 forbids the fields and AC-PTY-082 requires them. B3 is the screen's Input section; AC-PTY-082 asks that the fields be shown. The Customer read (API-PTY-002) carries `creditLimit` and `paymentTermDays` only while `b2bCredit` is on (REQ-PTY-071); the Customer update body (API-PTY-003, `CustomerUpdateRequest`) carries no credit field; credit is written only through API-PTY-017 / API-PTY-018 (SCR-PTY-003).

## Decision
- SCR-PTY-001 shows `creditLimit` and `paymentTermDays` as **read-only display values**, in a "Credit" group, only while `b2bCredit` is on and the values are present in the API-PTY-002 response.
- They are never inputs on SCR-PTY-001, never in its search filters or result columns, and never sent by its Save.
- The group carries an "Edit credit" «تعديل الائتمان» link to SCR-PTY-003 (`/pty/customer-credits/:customerId`), offered to users holding PERM_PTY_CUSTOMER_CREDIT_VIEW. Editing stays on SCR-PTY-003.
- While the flag is off the group is absent: 0 credit fields and 0 credit filters (AC-PTY-078).

## Why it is not breaking
B3 is respected: SCR-PTY-001 takes no credit input. AC-PTY-082 is respected: the fields are shown once the flag is on. AC-PTY-078 is respected: nothing is shown while it is off. No REQ, RULE, field or permission is added, and no locked decision changes.

## Consequences
- The ui-ux-spec block SCR-PTY-001 and the F1/F2/F3/F4 SUBs of SCR-PTY-001 carry the read-only group. The `CustomerFormValues` type excludes the credit fields.
- If a later SRS version wants credit to be edited on the Customer screen, that is a change to SCR-REQ-PTY-001 B3 and to the Customer update operation, not to this plan.

## Traces
SCR-PTY-001, SCR-PTY-003 · REQ-PTY-070, REQ-PTY-071, REQ-PTY-073 · AC-PTY-078, AC-PTY-082 · API-PTY-002, API-PTY-003, API-PTY-017

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-PTY-034.md>>>
# ADR-PTY-034 — Frontend binding decisions for PTY v1

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : P3.2 · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29

## Context
The P3.2 frontend plan is bound to `api-spec-pty.yaml` (37 operations). The SRS, the PRD and the document leave several frontend choices open. Each is decided below so that the implementer does not have to. None adds a field, rule or permission to the SRS.

## Decisions

1. **Reads outside the API document.** The screens need four things that are not operations of api-spec-pty.yaml: lookup values (given `erp-core` `mdl`: CUSTOMER_GROUP, ADDRESS_TYPE, CREDIT_OVERRUN_ACTION, CREDIT_CHECK_RESULT, CREDIT_OVERRIDE_STATUS — SRS A6, A9), the `b2bCredit` flag (given application configuration, `GET /api/public/app-config`), the session's permission names (given `sec`), and the name of the user who decided a Credit override request (given `sec` user read; the document's `CreditOverrideRequest.decidedBy` is an identifier). They are hooks of kind `lookup` or `init`, never `read`; the last one is UXD-PTY-001. No PTY operation is invented for them.

2. **Operations not bound to a PTY screen.** API-PTY-012 (read Address), API-PTY-033 (walk-in Customer), API-PTY-034 (guest Customer resolution), API-PTY-035 (credit check), API-PTY-036 (use Credit override request) and API-PTY-037 (`b2bCredit` switch-off dependency) are called by Sales & POS, Purchasing, Storefront or the capability-flag owner (SRS A8.1). No PTY screen calls them; they stay in the API binding with their REQs and appear in the operations coverage as consumer-only. REQ-PTY-052 and REQ-PTY-054 have no operation (in-process, ADR-PTY-025) and no frontend surface.

3. **Registration in place (REQ-PTY-008).** The Customer and Supplier screens export a Quick register sub-view (`CustomerQuickRegister`, `SupplierQuickRegister`) that a host document mounts in its own container. It is the Entry's primary field group (names, mobile, email) with one mandatory mark on the name group (AC-PTY-007, AC-PTY-021), one save (API-PTY-001 / API-PTY-006), and returns `{id, code}` to the host so the host screen stays open (AC-PTY-010, AC-PTY-011). It shows no customer group (the server sets RETAIL, REQ-PTY-007) and no address pane. The back-office Entry keeps the SRS B3 count (2 marks for Customers, 1 for Suppliers).

4. **One save with ordered calls.** Addresses are a child collection of a `page` container, so they sit inline; one line is edited in a one-line drawer that returns the line to the page's form. The screen's one Save sends the record call first (create or update) and, only after it succeeded, the address changes (API-PTY-014, API-PTY-013, API-PTY-011, then API-PTY-015) one after another; the address calls are not sent when no line changed. A refused record call sends nothing else.

5. **Commands are not saves.** Deactivate, Reactivate, Make supplier, Make customer, Clear credit, Approve, Reject and Cancel request are single confirmed calls. They are disabled while the screen's form holds unsaved changes, so no user leaves believing an unsent edit was saved with them.

6. **Refusals stay reachable.** Commands whose refusal the SRS tests are offered, not hidden: Deactivate and Make supplier on the walk-in Customer (AC-PTY-055, AC-PTY-057), Cancel request on a request the user did not create when the user holds DELETE (AC-PTY-109). The server's refusal message is shown.

7. **Cache policy deviations.** Lookups: `staleTime` 30 min, `gcTime` 60 min. Application configuration: refetched on every route mount (`staleTime` 0) so a `b2bCredit` change shows from the next screen load (REQ-PTY-073). Everything else uses the tanstack-query defaults.

8. **Credit history placement.** The credit history of SCR-PTY-003 is an inline read-only pane beneath the credit fields, paged with the body, with no save and no scroll region of its own.

9. **Removed (gate-analysis revise, G1 / G20).** The former PENDING interim for the Party named by RULE-PTY-002 is superseded by ADR-PTY-043: API-PTY-028 gains an email filter, and the action "Open that party" «فتح ذلك الطرف» finds the Party through the Customer search and then the Supplier search by email. This ADR holds no open item.

## Consequences
- The plan's API binding, F2 hooks, F4 routes and the ALIGN-FE operations coverage follow these decisions.
- No decision of this ADR is open; the RULE-PTY-002 action is decided in ADR-PTY-043.

## Traces
SCR-PTY-001, SCR-PTY-002, SCR-PTY-003, SCR-PTY-004, UXD-PTY-001 · REQ-PTY-002, REQ-PTY-007, REQ-PTY-008, REQ-PTY-013, REQ-PTY-030, REQ-PTY-031, REQ-PTY-033, REQ-PTY-035, REQ-PTY-073, REQ-PTY-103, REQ-PTY-108 · AC-PTY-007, AC-PTY-010, AC-PTY-011, AC-PTY-013, AC-PTY-021, AC-PTY-055, AC-PTY-057, AC-PTY-109 · API-PTY-001, API-PTY-006, API-PTY-011, API-PTY-012, API-PTY-013, API-PTY-014, API-PTY-015, API-PTY-033, API-PTY-034, API-PTY-035, API-PTY-036, API-PTY-037 · RULE-PTY-002

# ADR-PTY-035 — Tenant columns, version column and tenant-composite uniqueness on every PTY table

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : gate-analysis revise (G2, G7) · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Supersedes : ADR-PTY-021 · Revises : ADR-PTY-022 (seed column list)

## Context
ADR-PTY-021 left tenant scoping to the given and gave no PTY table a tenant column. The erp-core checklist does not allow that:
- C1: every table has `TENANT_ID BIGINT NOT NULL`, `FK_<TABLE>_TENANT → CORE_TENANT(ID)` and an index led by `TENANT_ID`, and every `UNIQUE` is composite with `TENANT_ID`;
- C2: every entity extends `com.erp.common.domain.AuditableEntity`;
- C5: lookup rows are seeded for `TENANT_ID = 1`.

`AuditableEntity` maps `TENANT_ID` (Hibernate `@TenantId`), `VERSION` (`@Version`) and the four audit columns (erp-core `common`, ADR-COMMON-003). An entity that extends it needs both columns in its table.

## Decision
1. Each of the five tables carries `TENANT_ID BIGINT NOT NULL`, `FK_<TABLE>_TENANT` → `CORE_TENANT(ID)` and an index `IDX_<TABLE>_TENANT` whose first column is `TENANT_ID`. It also carries `VERSION BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. All seven are new DBFs: TENANT_ID is DBF-PTY-068 … 072 and VERSION is DBF-PTY-073 … 077. Both are system columns that only `AuditableEntity` writes.
2. Every unique constraint and unique index leads with `TENANT_ID`. This includes the partial and expression indexes UQ_PTY_PARTY_EMAIL, UQ_PTY_CUSTOMER_IS_WALK_IN_FL, UQ_PTY_ADDRESS_IS_DEFAULT_FL and the new UQ_PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUEST_OPEN_SOURCE (ADR-PTY-042). Each per-tenant rule is therefore enforced per tenant by the database: RULE-PTY-002, 009, 014, 017, 020 and 034, and the business numbers of RULE-PTY-007 and 031.
3. Each parent carries `UQ_<TABLE>_TENANT_PK (TENANT_ID, <PK>)`, and each intra-module FK is composite `(TENANT_ID, <FK>)`, so that a child can only point to a parent of its own tenant.
4. Every query names the tenant. JPQL, derived and search-builder queries run under the given tenant filter. The native queries QR-PTY-011 and QR-PTY-037 name `TENANT_ID = :tenantId` themselves and carry `@TenantUnscoped(reason, adr = "ADR-PTY-027")`.
5. The BLOCK 8 seeds write the given tables with `TENANT_ID = 1` (PLATFORM), using the column names erp-core 1.6.0 writes in its own seeds. These are `KEY` and `OWNER_MODULE_CODE` on MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE, `LOOKUP_TYPE_ID` resolved by key on MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE, and the CAT module's form. New tenants receive copies through the given provisioning. Flyway runs the migration in its own transaction, so the block holds no `BEGIN` and no `COMMIT`.
6. Bodies do not carry `VERSION`. Every PTY write loads and saves its row inside one transaction under the row locks of ADR-PTY-026, so the version check never fails for a PTY caller. It stays the given backstop against a detached write.

## Consequences
- The DBF count goes from 67 to 79: 5 TENANT_ID, 5 VERSION, and 2 CURRENCY_CODE (ADR-PTY-037).
- A record of another tenant reads and writes as not found. The PTY-404-* rows say "in the caller's tenant".
- ADR-PTY-022's instruction to check the column list at execution is replaced by the column list above.

## Traces
ENT-PTY-001 … ENT-PTY-005 · DBF-PTY-068 … DBF-PTY-077 · RULE-PTY-002, 007, 009, 014, 017, 020, 031, 034 · QR-PTY-011, QR-PTY-037 · REQ-PTY-010, REQ-PTY-044, REQ-PTY-054

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-PTY-036 — Number series and the approver notification template are seeded by the PTY migration

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : gate-analysis revise (G21, G6) · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Revises : ADR-PTY-029 (bootstrap — number series and notification template)

## Context
ADR-PTY-029 registered the series PTY_PARTY and PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE through `NumberSeriesApi` from PTY's `TenantProvisioningContributor`. The db-script (D-P2-07) seeded no `CORE_NUMBER_SERIES` row. The approver notification of API-PTY-019 was sent as inline text.

The erp-core checklist does not allow either:
- C9: every document number is `NumberSeriesApi.next(code)` from a `CORE_NUMBER_SERIES` row seeded in `V1000+`, and it is stored in a column unique with `TENANT_ID`;
- C8: every message is `NotificationDispatchApi.dispatch(DispatchCommand)` with a `NOTIF_TEMPLATE` code seeded in `V1000+`.

## Decision
1. db-script BLOCK 8c seeds two `CORE_NUMBER_SERIES` rows for `TENANT_ID = 1`. Both use pattern `{PREFIX}-{SEQ:6}` and reset policy `NEVER`:
   - `PTY_PARTY`, prefix `P`, gives P-000120 (DBF-PTY-007);
   - `PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE`, prefix `CO`, gives CO-000031 (DBF-PTY-061).
   New tenants receive copies with the counter at 1 through the given provisioning.
2. UQ_PTY_PARTY_CODE is `(TENANT_ID, CODE)` and UQ_PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUEST_DOC_NO is `(TENANT_ID, DOC_NO)` (ADR-PTY-035).
3. db-script BLOCK 8d seeds the `NOTIF_TEMPLATE` row `PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUESTED` for `TENANT_ID = 1`, channel IN_APP and category UTILITY. Its variables are `{docNo}` and `{name}`. Its body is:
   - ar «طلب تجاوز حد الائتمان {docNo} للعميل {name} بانتظار موافقتك.»
   - en «Credit override request {docNo} for {name} is waiting for your approval.»
   The given copies it to new tenants.
4. API-PTY-019 dispatches one `DispatchCommand(recipientId = the approver's sec user id, templateCode = "PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUESTED", channelHint = IN_APP, moduleCode = "PTY", referenceId = creditOverrideRequestPk, referenceType = "PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUEST", variables = {docNo, name})` per approver. PTY formats no subject or body.
5. PTY's `TenantProvisioningContributor` now creates only the walk-in Customer (REQ-PTY-044). It no longer registers a series.

## Consequences
- The `bootstrap` block names the migration as the producer of both series and of the template.
- When dispatch runs is decided in the backend plan's CORE (after commit, on the given event executor — G9).

## Traces
DBF-PTY-007, DBF-PTY-061 · RULE-PTY-007, RULE-PTY-031 · REQ-PTY-006, REQ-PTY-092, REQ-PTY-093 · API-PTY-001, 006, 019, 033, 034

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-PTY-037.md>>>
# ADR-PTY-037 — A currency code on every credit amount, hidden while the tenant has one currency

Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking) · Stage : gate-analysis revise (G11, CM-8) · Module : PTY v1 · Date : 2026-10-29
Supersedes : ADR-PTY-020 · Depends on : CORE-GAP-tenant-base-currency (OPEN)

## Context
ADR-PTY-020 left the credit amounts without a currency column and cited the scope exception "multi-currency party balances". The same approved scope exception says: "the currency dimension exists in the model, hidden while its count is 1". Upstream wins (GOVERNANCE-CORE §1), so the dimension has to exist in the model now (profile check CM-8). The currency stays hidden in the UI.

## Decision
1. `CURRENCY_CODE VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL` (an ISO 4217 code) is added in two places:
   - on PTY_CUSTOMER (DBF-PTY-078, ENT-PTY-002.currencyCode) — the currency of creditLimit and of the Customer's open exposure;
   - on PTY_CREDIT_OVERRIDE_REQUEST (DBF-PTY-079, ENT-PTY-005.currencyCode) — the currency of saleAmount, creditLimitAtRequest and openExposure.
   It is a system field and is never accepted from a caller in v1.
2. **Value.** The column holds the tenant base currency at the time the row is created. A request copies the currency of its Customer. erp-core 1.6.0 publishes no read of a tenant's base currency: the ledger currencies in `GL_TENANT_CURRENCY` have no published interface, and neither `cu` nor `tenant` names one. Until CORE-GAP-tenant-base-currency is answered, PTY reads it through `SettingsApi.getOrDefault("PTY_BASE_CURRENCY_CODE", String.class, "XXX")`. `PTY_BASE_CURRENCY_CODE` is a PTY setting (checklist C14), set per tenant at setup through `/api/v1/common/configurations`. While the tenant has not set it, rows are written with `XXX`, the ISO 4217 code for "no currency involved". v1 holds one currency per tenant (the scope exception), so no computation in v1 reads the column to convert.
3. **Credit check and requests.** Amounts are compared in the Customer's currency. The credit check response, the credit standing, the credit list and the request responses carry `currencyCode`. A consumer converts its sale amount into that currency before a check, a request or a use, as before.
4. **UI.** The frontend does not show `currencyCode` while the tenant has one currency. Amounts are formatted in that currency.

## Consequences
- The DBF matrix, the API schemas `Customer`, `CustomerCredit`, `CustomerCreditRow`, `CreditCheckResult`, `CreditOverrideRequest` and `CreditOverrideRow` all gain `currencyCode`, and so do contract items CON-PTY-002, 005, 009, 015, 017 and 022. All of these are additive.
- When the core answers the gap, a delta reads the given source instead of the setting, and one migration re-stamps `XXX` rows with the tenant's base currency. When multi-currency ships (wave 4), a request may then carry a currency other than its Customer's, through a new rule.

## Traces
ENT-PTY-002.currencyCode, ENT-PTY-005.currencyCode · DBF-PTY-078, DBF-PTY-079 · REQ-PTY-064, REQ-PTY-079, REQ-PTY-085, REQ-PTY-091 · API-PTY-002, 016, 017, 019, 020, 030, 032, 035

<<<END ADR>>>
